title: Dynamic kernel steering and speculative replay for stable multi-stream decode
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: We see intermittent CUDA graph capture failures and non-deterministic replay correctness during concurrent prefill+decode workloads on multi-stream nodes. This ticket implements a dynamic kernel steering layer plus a lightweight speculative-replay validator to improve capture stability and ensure deterministic outputs across replays while preserving throughput targets. The work focuses on (1) selecting safer kernel variants for capture windows, (2) sequencing prefill boundaries to avoid mixed-occupancy races, and (3) a low-overhead replay validation pass that detects divergence and falls back to uncaptured execution for the affected requests.
acceptance_criteria: Graph capture failure rate for mixed prefill+decode workload reduced to <0.1% over 24h test run on our 8xA100 staging fleet
P99 latency regression for steady-state decode workloads <= 2% compared to baseline (no speculative validation enabled), measured across three sequence-length profiles
Replay divergence detection catches >99% of injected mismatch faults in unit/integration tests and triggers fallback path without impacting unrelated streams
Rollout toggle (console + config flag) to enable/disable speculative replay validator per pool and a clear dashboard metric for 'replay-fallbacks'
technical_notes: Kernel steering: add a mid-layer that maps attention/softmax GEMM kernels to 'capture-safe' variants when in a capture window. Capture-safe variants prioritize deterministic shared-memory use and avoid async workspace allocation patterns.

Heuristic: use occupancy + sequence-length histogram to mark kernels 'safe' or 'risky'. For risky cases (high-mixed-quant or variable sequence lengths) choose fallback kernel that uses explicit barrier points compatible with CUDA graph capture semantics.

Prefill sequencing: introduce a small prefill quiesce period (configurable, default 0ms) where prefill completion waits for outstanding stream-prefetches to drain before entering a graph capture. This reduces inter-stream KV cache races for large batch prefills.

Speculative replay validator: after graph replay, compute a compact 64-bit rolling checksum of key intermediate tensors (attention outputs + KV summary) and compare against a golden checksum produced by a deterministic single-stream uncaptured execution during staged rollout samples. On mismatch, mark request for fallback to uncaptured path and emit traces for investigation.

Determinism: enforce deterministic RNG and remove use of atomic add for index counters inside capture windows. For atomic ops that break determinism, provide a per-kernel emulation with mutexed counters when capture is active.
Performance: validator runs in-band but only for sampling fraction (configurable, default 0.5% of requests) to limit overhead. Metric 'validator-latency' will be recorded separately in console.
Testing: add synthetic fuzz harness that randomizes sequence lengths, token arrival jitter, and mixed quantized model variants. Integrate with CI to run nightly stress tests on preemptible nodes.

Fallback flow: on a replay mismatch, we will retry the request once on uncaptured code path with exact same inputs and surface a 'replay-fallback' event to the trace and billing logs. Ensure request-level idempotency semantics are preserved.
plan: Week 1 (2025-02-14 to 2025-02-21): design kernel-safe mapping API and prefill quiesce hook; prototype kernel flags in dev runtime
Week 2 (2025-02-22 to 2025-02-28): implement speculative replay checksum and lightweight validator sampling; add tracing points; unit tests
Week 3 (2025-03-01 to 2025-03-07): end-to-end stress tests on staging fleet; iterate heuristics for kernel selection; telemetry dashboard for replay-fallbacks
Week 4 (2025-03-08 to 2025-03-14): gradual rollout behind feature flag to 10% of production pools; monitor capture-failure and p99 latency; prepare roll-back plan
Post-rollout: gather metrics for a 2-week observation window then finalize defaults and documentation
risks: Validator sampling introduces measurement bias if sample selection correlates with traffic patterns; mitigate by stratified sampling across pools and model families
Fallback to uncaptured path increases pressure on kernels not optimized for uncaptured latency; need autoscaling guardrails to avoid overloading nodes
Changing kernel selection may expose performance cliffs for rare model architectures; will gate aggressive changes behind canary policy per-model
Rolling back RNG/determinism changes can be invasive; we must ensure backward compatibility with saved KV cache formats
